topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text: The envelope lay on the floor, a slipped stitch in the fabric of the day. It wasn’t mine, but the address was here—now. The handwriting, wavering and unsure, belonged to someone else, someone who once breathed life into these walls. I traced the lines, the curves telling stories I never heard. The corners of the paper were worn, like the edges of a map leading to a place I couldn’t visit. I couldn’t shake the weight of it, the quiet insistence that this was a message not for me, yet it found me. The silence of the room pressed in, each shadow deeper, each whisper louder. I didn’t open it, couldn’t. It felt like a secret, a private pact with the shadows. Outside, the sky deepened, the world holding its breath.
